title: Cadence mosaic: staggered regional windows & rollback heuristics (draft)
body:
Context and purpose:

This is a working draft of a release cadence 'mosaic' that we can use for multi-region, low-risk rollouts. The idea is to treat deploys as a set of timeboxed 'slots' (orbital lanes) that can be stitched together across regions and customer tiers. This doc is intentionally practical: a short checklist, a compact 7-day rolling calendar pattern we can copy, and a candidate rollback/containment heuristic set for common failure modes.

Scope:
- Applies to feature, model-variant, and infra rollouts that can be staged by region/tier.
- Not for emergency hotfixes (see emergency-runbook).

High-level design principles (TL;DR):
- Small slots: prefer 1–3 hour windows per cohort to limit blast radius.
- Staggered region cadence: avoid simultaneous cross-region warmups.
- Canary with traffic-shed gating: use metrics-driven holdpoints (latency P95, error-rate, token-per-request delta).
- Fast rollback lanes: pre-defined rollback artifacts (previous model image, infra snapshot, routing policy) should be addressed in the deploy plan.

Release slot pattern (7-day repeating example):
- Day 0 (Mon): Internal canary in non-prod mimic (20% synthetic traffic).
- Day 1 (Tue): Narrow prod canary in region A (1–2% users). Hold 2 hours.
- Day 2 (Wed): Regional ramp in region A to 20% with KV-cache priming. Hold 3 hours.
- Day 3 (Thu): Canary in region B with gated fallback route to region A.
- Day 4 (Fri): Weekend-safe ramp in region A and B to 60% if metrics green.
- Day 5 (Sat): Selective enterprise-tier ramp (manual opt-in) for dedicated customers.
- Day 6 (Sun): Quiet window and sampling; decision point for broad rollout on Mon.

Suggested calendar / slot names for quick reference:
- internal-mirror, prod-canary-a, ramp-a, prod-canary-b, ramp-b, enterprise-optin, quiet-sampling

Preflight checklist (complete before any prod slot):
- [ ] CI green and no critical regressions in last 72h.
- [ ] Smoke test suite (core generation, KV-cache sanity) passed on the exact build to be deployed.
- [ ] Canary config created in release-manager (route weights, TTLs).
- [ ] Observability dashboard tabs: latency, error-rate, mem/gpu util, token-rate, trailing eval quality.
- [ ] Linked artifacts listed (PR, Jira, confluence) in the release ticket.
- [ ] Runbook owner and standby rotation assigned for the 24h window.

Day-of slot checklist (operator):
- [ ] Confirm deploy bundle checksum and image tag.
- [ ] Set maintenance routing policy and brief SRE on fallback lane.
- [ ] Start slot timer and note t=0 in the release ticket.
- [ ] After 15 minutes, check metric snapshots vs baseline (latency P95, 99, error-rate).
- [ ] At 60m, check qualitative signals (smoke prompts, sample outputs for hallucination/regression).
- [ ] If any gate fails, execute containment (see heuristics). Document decision in ticket.
- [ ] If slot completes clean, publish short 'slot green' note to #release-ops and update ticket.

Rollback / containment heuristics (fast lanes):
- Severity A (incident-level: backend errors >0.5% absolute or latency P95 >2x baseline): immediate rollback to last-green and page SRE + product.
- Severity B (quality regressions: generation hallucination or significant embedding drift detected by eval harness): pause ramp, revert routing for affected cohorts, and launch triage.
- Severity C (resource anomalies: GPU OOMs, sustained memory leak): throttle traffic, scale down new variant, enable fallback model variant.

Rollback nouns (what to have ready):
- previous-image-tag (string)
- route-fallback-policy id
- snapshot/timepoint for infra state
- alert runbook link

Decision matrix (quick):
- Error-rate spike AND cross-region correlated -> Severity A -> immediate rollback.
- Localized quality signal in single cohort -> Severity B -> pause ramp + targeted revert.
- Intermittent CPU/GPU spike only during heavy tails -> Severity C -> throttle + investigate kernel queue depth.

Observability and signals (recommended monitors):
- Latency P50/P95/P99 (text-gen tokens/sec normalized), per-model and per-route.
- Error-rate (5m and 1m), per-region and per-instance type.
- Token-cost delta (new vs baseline), to detect runaway generation costs.
- Evaluations: run short-consensus eval set for a 100 sample prompt set every slot. Flag >5% drop in pass rate.

Release notes (candidate draft for internal audience):
- Title: incremental-model-routing: multi-region staggered rollout (v2026.05.10)
- Summary: Deploys model-variant v2026.05.10 with improved KV-cache priming and reduced prefix latency for short sequences. Adds a new routing policy to enable gradual per-region ramp.
- Changes: 
  - runtime: fix for attention cache eviction bug under continuous-batching (reduces cold-start tail latency).
  - serving: introduce route weight config for per-customer cohort opt-in.
  - infra: additional autoscaler tuning to avoid oscillations during short ramps.
- Known limitations / gotchas: 
  - Small number of long-context requests (>12k tokens) may see higher memory pressure; monitor jobs with tag: long-context.
  - Enterprise customers with pinned quantized models will remain on pinned path until manual opt-in.
- Migration notes for SRE/Platform: 
  - Ensure previous-image-tag v2026.04.29 is cached in the region broker; quick-redeploy instructions included in the runbook.
  - Run short-consensus eval on a copy of production prompts post-slot.

Open questions / TODOs (needs decisions):
- Do we want a hard max-slot-size policy (e.g., no slot >3h) or allow exceptions for bulk migration? (Priya to propose).
- Should enterprise opt-in be automated via subscription flag or manual by Account Exec? (Product decision needed).
- Validate that autoscaler tuning doesn’t impact dedicated pools (Ethan to run a synthetic load scenario).

Quick links (for on-call):
- Runbook: Confluence: Cadence mosaic (see linked artifacts).
- Jira: RINF-4123 (canary gating), RINF-4140 (autoscaler tweak).
- PR: GH#2318 (runtime fix).

Notes to self (fragile bits):
- Keep the quiet-sampling day light on traffic; the goal is signal collection not user exposure.
- Document the exact eval prompt set and add to the release ticket each time.

If the group likes this pattern I can:
1) turn the slot names into a templated release-manager config (JSON) that we can import, and
2) prototype an automated holdpoint checker that marks slots green/fail from metric thresholds.

Feedback thread: please drop comments in the Confluence page or ping in #release-ops.
